label: Do flat strike bonuses get the weapon multiplier?
short: Backstab, Ambush, Mutilate and Holy Strike add a flat bonus. Is it multiplied with the weapon damage, or added after?
description: These strikes deal a percent of weapon damage plus a flat bonus. Forever's client adds the bonus before the percent, so it is multiplied too; Forever's tooltips print it as if it were added after. Added after, Backstab (150%) and Ambush lose damage, while Mutilate (75%) and Holy Strike (50%) gain.
source: Forever client 1.60.1.70338 (effect order); Era's server adds the bonus first on the same Backstab data. No beta log shows it yet.

settings.label: Added after (tooltip)
settings.rationale: Forever's tooltips read literally.

settings.label: Multiplied too (client)
settings.rationale: The client's effect order, and Era's server rule on the same data.

label: Can off-hand hits proc Windfury Totem?
short: Forever's totem is a party aura with no weapon rule. In Era, only main-hand hits could proc it.
description: Whether off-hand hits can proc Windfury Totem. In Era the totem put an enchant on the main hand, so only main-hand hits procced it. Forever's totem is a party aura with nothing tying it to a weapon. The totem needs level 32, beyond the beta, so nobody has checked.
source: Forever client builds 70291 and 70338 (party aura, no weapon condition).

settings.label: Main hand only (Era)
settings.value: only main-hand hits can proc it
settings.rationale: How Era worked: the totem enchanted the main hand.

settings.label: Any melee hit
settings.value: main-hand and off-hand hits can proc it
settings.rationale: Forever's party aura names no weapon.

label: Does Rage from hits grow with level?
short: Forever's Rage per white hit depends on weapon speed, measured only up to level 30. Growth to 60 is unknown.
description: Forever gives Rage from a white hit by weapon speed, not damage. Beta testers measured the amount up to level 30. Kept flat at 60, a swing gives about half of Classic's Rage; nobody knows if it grows with level.
source: Blizzard's Priest & Warrior deep dive; beta testers' level 30 measurements (forum thread 2355684). Model: Rage = k × weapon speed, k(L) = k30 × (1 + s × (L − 30) / 30).

settings.label: Flat (level 30 value)
settings.value: Rage per hit stays at its level 30 value
settings.rationale: No growth: about half of Classic's Rage per swing.

settings.label: Halfway (×1.5 at 60)
settings.rationale: Halfway between flat and Classic-like.

settings.label: Like Classic (×2 at 60)
settings.rationale: Close to Classic's Rage per swing at 60.

label: Do off-hand hits give full Rage?
short: Does an off-hand hit give as much Rage as a main-hand hit of the same speed? Nobody has measured it.
description: Forever's Rage per hit depends on the weapon's speed. Blizzard said nothing about the off hand, and nobody has measured it. TBC's similar formula gave the off hand half.
source: Blizzard's Priest & Warrior deep dive (no off-hand rule stated).

settings.label: Half (like TBC)
settings.rationale: TBC's formula gave the off hand half.

settings.label: Full
settings.rationale: Blizzard stated no off-hand penalty.

label: Extra Rage from critical white hits
short: Blizzard first said crits give 75% more Rage, then 100% in a second pass the same day.
description: Under Forever, a critical white hit gives extra Rage. Blizzard's 1 October warrior notes said 75%, and the second warrior pass that day said 100%. No beta log has checked it.
source: Blizzard's warrior development notes, 1 October (two passes).

settings.label: +75% (first note)
settings.value: a white crit gives 75% more Rage
settings.rationale: Blizzard's first number.

settings.label: +100% (later note)
settings.value: a white crit gives twice the Rage
settings.rationale: The later pass, the same day.

label: How much attack power Rend gets
short: Blizzard says Rend now scales significantly with attack power, but the client gives no number.
description: Blizzard's notes say Rend got significant attack power scaling, but the client holds no coefficient. The presets add a modest 2% of attack power to each tick; the other settings use none or a larger share.
source: Blizzard's warrior development notes; Forever client 70338 (no coefficient).

settings.label: None (client)
settings.rationale: The client as it is.

settings.label: Small (2% a tick)
settings.rationale: A modest share: about 14% of attack power over a full Rend.

settings.label: Large (5% a tick)
settings.rationale: About 35% of attack power over a full Rend.

label: How much the pet inherits from the hunter
short: The pet gets 10% of the hunter's ranged attack power, measured to level 30. Does it get the hunter's hit?
description: The beta measured the pet's share of the hunter's ranged attack power at 10%, at levels 20 to 30. Blizzard says the pet also takes the hunter's hit, without a number. The sim gives it all of it, as Season of Discovery did.
source: ForeverChanges' hunter pets page and the forever-hunter wiki (attack power); Blizzard's 17 September known issues (hit).

settings.label: 10% AP, no hit
settings.value: 10% of ranged attack power, none of the hunter's hit
settings.rationale: Only what the beta measured.

settings.label: 10% AP + hit
settings.value: 10% of ranged attack power plus the hunter's hit
settings.rationale: The measured attack power, plus the hit Blizzard's known issues mention.

settings.label: 22% AP + hit (SoD)
settings.value: 22% of ranged attack power plus the hunter's hit
settings.rationale: Season of Discovery's values for the same aura.

label: Do fast pets hit as hard as slow pets?
short: On the beta every pet hits like a 2.0 sec pet, so the 1.0 sec cat wins. The presets treat it as a bug.
description: On the beta, a pet's hit is the size of a 2.0 sec pet's hit whatever its attack speed, so the fastest pet (the 1.0 sec cat) deals the most. Nobody knows if that is intended. The presets treat it as a bug: Classic's rule, where a pet's hit scales with its attack speed and every pet's white damage is the same.
source: Beta players, on ForeverChanges' hunter pets page and the forever-hunter wiki.

settings.label: Scales with speed (Classic)
settings.value: a fast pet's hits are smaller
settings.rationale: Classic's rule, if the beta's behaviour is a bug.

settings.label: Same hit (beta)
settings.value: every pet hits like a 2.0 sec pet
settings.rationale: The only behaviour seen on the beta.

label: Trueshot Aura and Hunter's Mark at 60
short: Both spells' top ranks are weaker than the rank before. The presets assume Blizzard fixes them.
description: In the client, the top ranks of Trueshot Aura and Hunter's Mark give less attack power than the rank before them. The presets assume Blizzard fixes the top ranks onto the curve before release. Otherwise a hunter casts the stronger older rank, or, at worst, only the weaker top ranks count.
source: Forever client 70338 (Trueshot Aura 30 / 40 / 50 / 75 / 50, Hunter's Mark 26 / 59 / 98 / 71).

settings.label: Top ranks as written
settings.value: Trueshot Aura +50, Hunter's Mark +71 attack power
settings.rationale: If only the weaker top ranks can be used.

settings.label: Best older rank
settings.value: Trueshot Aura +75, Hunter's Mark +98 attack power
settings.rationale: A player casts the stronger lower rank.

settings.label: Top ranks fixed
settings.value: Trueshot Aura +100, Hunter's Mark +140 attack power
settings.rationale: Blizzard fixes the top ranks onto the curve.

label: Hunter crit per Agility at 60
short: At level 1, Forever's hunter gets 22% more crit per Agility than Classic's. Does that hold at 60?
description: At level 1 on the beta, a hunter gets 22% more crit from each point of Agility than in Classic. The other classes match Classic, so Forever changed the hunter's table on purpose. How it carries to 60 is unknown; the presets carry the level 1 ratio to 60.
source: Beta character sheets at level 1 (notes.md, 10 October).

settings.label: Classic's (53 Agility a 1%)
settings.rationale: The level 1 difference stays a level 1 quirk.

settings.label: 22% more (beta)
settings.value: 22% more crit per Agility than Classic
settings.rationale: The beta's level 1 ratio, carried to 60.

label: Will Raptor Strike's top rank get a raise?
short: Raptor Strike's flat bonus past level 30 sits far below Era, unlike its level 24 rank. Not retuned yet?
description: Raptor Strike's level 24 rank keeps 0.88 of Era's flat bonus, but the ranks past level 30 sit at 0.50 to 0.70, as if not retuned yet. The preset casts the top rank at +96, halfway there; the settings change that bonus.
source: Forever client 70338 (rank tuning audit).

settings.label: No raise (+70)
settings.rationale: The client value.

settings.label: Halfway (+96)
settings.rationale: A partial retune.

settings.label: Full raise (+123)
settings.rationale: Kept at the level 24 rank's 0.88 of Era.

label: Does Seal of Righteousness count spell power twice?
short: Season of Discovery's seal added spell power twice per hit. Forever's client has the same data; untested.
description: In Season of Discovery, each Seal of Righteousness hit counted the paladin's spell power twice. Forever's client has the same seal data, so the sim does the same. A level 30 paladin with and without spell power would settle it.
source: Season of Discovery sim tests; Forever client spells 20286 and the seal's proc.

settings.label: Once
settings.value: 10% of spell power a hit, no two-hander bonus
settings.rationale: The proc spell's own coefficient, read plainly.

settings.label: Twice (like SoD)
settings.value: 2 × 11% of spell power a hit with a two-hander
settings.rationale: Measured in Season of Discovery on the same data.

label: Does Seal of Righteousness's spell power grow with weapon speed?
short: Each Seal of Righteousness hit adds the same spell power whatever the weapon speed. In TBC, slower weapons got more.
description: Each Seal of Righteousness hit adds a share of the paladin's spell power. The sim gives every hit the same share, whatever the weapon speed, as Season of Discovery and Era measured. In TBC the share grew with weapon speed. The presets swing a 3.4 sec two-hander, so the difference is small.
source: Season of Discovery and Era measurements (flat per swing); TBC's Seal of Righteousness (scaled with speed).

settings.label: Scales with weapon speed (TBC-like)
settings.value: spell power share × weapon speed ÷ 3.6 sec (two-hander) or ÷ 2.4 sec (one-hander)
settings.rationale: If Forever adopted TBC's speed-scaled seal.

settings.label: Flat per swing
settings.value: the same spell power share every hit
settings.rationale: What Season of Discovery and Era measured on the same seal.

label: Consecration's spell power bonus
short: How much spell power each Consecration tick gets. The only Forever number comes from an old tooltip.
description: Consecration's damage runs through a server script, and no page shows how much spell power a tick gets. The only Forever number is 9.5% a tick, from an older tooltip. At the presets' spell power, that is about two thirds of each tick.
source: An older Forever tooltip; Era's value is 4.2% a tick.

settings.label: Era's (4.2%)
settings.rationale: Era's value, if the old tooltip was a leftover.

settings.label: Old tooltip (9.5%)
settings.rationale: The only Forever number anyone has seen.

label: Does Two-Handed Spec boost Holy seal damage?
short: The client's Two-Handed Weapon Specialization names Physical damage only. Era's servers also boost the Holy seal procs.
description: Two-Handed Weapon Specialization raises damage done with a two-hander. The client lists Physical damage only, which leaves out the Holy damage of the seal procs and Judgement of Command. Era's servers apply it to them anyway, and the sim follows Era.
source: Forever client spell 20111 (Physical only, the same as Era's); the Era sim.

settings.label: Physical only
settings.value: white hits and Holy Strike only
settings.rationale: The client data taken at its word.

settings.label: Seals too (Era)
settings.value: also seal procs and Judgement of Command
settings.rationale: How Era's servers treat the same talent.

label: Will Holy Strike and Consecration's top ranks shrink?
short: Past level 30, Holy Strike's flat bonus and Consecration grow much faster than below it, as if not retuned.
description: Up to level 30 (the beta cap), Holy Strike's flat bonus and Consecration grow slowly. Past 30 they jump, as if Blizzard hadn't retuned those ranks yet. Low cuts them back to the level 30 trend.
source: Forever client 70338 and Wowhead Forever (rank tuning audit).

settings.label: Cut to level 30 trend
settings.rationale: If Blizzard retunes them onto the level 30 curve.

settings.label: Client values
settings.value: the ranks as the client has them
settings.rationale: No rank past 30 changed in any beta build.

label: Can Seal of Command hits proc Windfury?
short: Can a Seal of Command hit (or Twist of Light's Echo of Command) proc Windfury Totem? Server side.
description: Whether the extra hit from Seal of Command, or from Twist of Light's Echo of Command, can proc Windfury Totem. Proc rules are set on the server, and the totem is beyond the beta's level cap. Only the twisting presets use Seal of Command.
source: The sim's melee proc rules; no beta log.

settings.label: No
settings.value: seal hits never proc the totem
settings.rationale: If the server counts seal hits as procs, which can't proc.

settings.label: Yes
settings.value: seal hits can proc the totem
settings.rationale: The sim's melee proc rules.

label: How often Maelstrom Weapon procs
short: The server sets Maelstrom Weapon's proc rate, and the talent needs level 34, beyond the beta.
description: Maelstrom Weapon builds stacks on melee hits; at 5 stacks Enhancement casts an instant Lightning Bolt. The client leaves the proc rate to the server, and the talent needs level 34, so nobody has tested it. The settings are procs a minute with 5/5 talent points.
source: Season of Discovery's rune code (wowsims/sod).

settings.label: 5 a minute
settings.rationale: Half the analogues. The weakest-grounded value here.

settings.label: 10 a minute (SoD)
settings.rationale: Season of Discovery's base rate.

settings.label: 15 a minute

The presets (Elemental, and Enhancement's Maelstrom Weapon bolts) cast rank 10 at ×1.12, that raise; the settings scale it.

settings.label: No raise
settings.rationale: The client.

settings.label: Halfway (+8%)

settings.label: Full raise (+16%)

label: How often Omen of Clarity procs
